title: Canonical convolution first page before identification with Tor
statement: For any commutative ring R and normalized filtered-page localization data d [def-kun-filtered-page-localization-data], bounded derived module objects C,D admit a filtered-derived realization U whose filtered cohomology identifies with a filtration on H^n(C tensor^L D). Its underlying map is H^n(f tensor^L g). The normalized page-one object at (-q,p+2q) is naturally the coproduct over i+j=q of H^p(single_0(H^i(C)) tensor^L single_0(H^j(D))) [lem-kun-derived-module-tor-comparison]. The induced first-page map is the coproduct of the two-variable tensor cohomology maps. No Tor or convergence is asserted.

source.place: Stacks Project More on Algebra Tags 0H7X, 0H7Y and 0H7Z, normalized E1 formula before Tor identification

proof.text: Take the canonical graded tensor realization and its normalized forgetful and graded comparisons. Compare d.Hbar followed by forgetting with omega followed by ordinary cohomology: their precompositions by the finite filtered quotient are naturally isomorphic through cochain cohomology. Full faithful precomposition descends this comparison. Compose it with cohomology of the underlying tensor isomorphism.

Transport each filtration by the resulting actual module isomorphism, defining its steps as subobjects represented by the old inclusions followed by that isomorphism. Construct the filtered isomorphism using Subobject.underlyingIso. Conjugate d.Hbar of a bifunctor map by these filtered isomorphisms. Naturality of the cohomology comparison and underlying tensor comparison gives exactly H^n(f tensor^L g).

Define the functor evaluating a spectral sequence at page one and (a,b). Its composite with d.Sbar and the functor gr^a followed by H^{a+b} agree after precomposition with the finite filtered quotient: use d.eS, the normalized finite filtered first-page isomorphism and its chain naturality, graded normalization, and ordinary homologyFunctorFactors. Descend this natural isomorphism by full faithful precomposition. Associated grading is functorial by uniqueness after composing with the cokernel projection.

Compose page-one-to-graded-cohomology with the graded tensor formula. Put a=-q and b=p+2q, so a+b+a=p and -a=q. Transport both isomorphisms and their naturality equations along these integer equalities. This produces the required coproduct first-page formula and map equation.

theorem exists_kunnethCanonicalFirstPage (d : FilteredPageLocalizationData R) :
    let P (p q : ℤ) (C D : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ModuleCat.{u} R :=
      ∐ fun ij : {ij : ℤ × ℤ // ij.1 + ij.2 = q} ↦
        ((kunnethModuleTensorHomology R p).obj
            ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.1).obj C.obj)).obj
          ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.2).obj D.obj)
    let m (p q : ℤ) {C C' D D' : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
        (f : C ⟶ C') (g : D ⟶ D') : P p q C D ⟶ P p q C' D' :=
      Limits.Sigma.map fun ij ↦
        ((kunnethModuleTensorHomology R p).map
            ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.1).map f.hom)).app
            ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.2).obj D.obj) ≫
          ((kunnethModuleTensorHomology R p).obj
            ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.1).obj C'.obj)).map
            ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) ij.val.2).map g.hom)
    ∃ (U : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤
          finiteFilteredModuleDerivedCategory R)
      (F : ∀ (C D : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (n : ℤ),
        DecreasingFiltration ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj (C.obj ⊗ D.obj)))
      (eH : ∀ (C D : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (n : ℤ),
        (d.Hbar n).obj ((U.obj C).obj D) ≅
          (⟨(homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj (C.obj ⊗ D.obj),
            F C D n⟩ : FilteredObject (ModuleCat.{u} R)))
      (e₁ : ∀ (C D : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (p q : ℤ),
        ((d.Sbar.obj ((U.obj C).obj D)).page 1).X (-q, p + 2 * q) ≅ P p q C D),
      (∀ (C C' D D' : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : C ⟶ C') (g : D ⟶ D')
          (p q : ℤ),
        ((d.Sbar.map ((U.map f).app D ≫ (U.obj C').map g)).hom 1).f (-q, p + 2 * q) ≫
            (e₁ C' D' p q).hom =
          (e₁ C D p q).hom ≫ m p q f g) ∧
      (∀ (C C' D D' : Bounded (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : C ⟶ C') (g : D ⟶ D') (n : ℤ),
        ∃ h : (⟨(homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj (C.obj ⊗ D.obj), F C D n⟩ :
            FilteredObject (ModuleCat.{u} R)) ⟶
          ⟨(homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj (C'.obj ⊗ D'.obj), F C' D' n⟩,
          h.hom = (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).map (f.hom ⊗ₘ g.hom) ∧
          (d.Hbar n).map ((U.map f).app D ≫ (U.obj C').map g) ≫ (eH C' D' n).hom =
            (eH C D n).hom ≫ h)
